## SECTION 0 — ANALYST'S PREAMBLE & HOW TO READ THIS REPORT

**The single most important fact in this pack is that ANAB is no longer the company that filed the FY2015–FY2025 financials.** The April 20, 2026 spin-off of First Tracks Biotherapeutics (Nasdaq: TRAX) transferred the biopharma pipeline (rosnilimab, ANB033, ANB101) out of ANAB. Today's ANAB is a **virtual royalty-management company** whose sole meaningful asset is a contractual royalty on GSK's Jemperli (dostarlimab), with a potential second royalty on Vanda's imsidolimab (PDUFA December 12, 2026). Every historical metric in Sections 3–6 of the pack — revenue, R&D, the FY2025 net loss of –$13M — contains the spun-off operations and **must not be extrapolated forward**.

We also note a second structural break: ANAB **shifted its fiscal year-end from December 31 to June 30**, effective July 1, 2026 (Trefis company page, [Estimate]). The next annual report will be a transition-period filing; quarterly comparability is compromised.

This report applies the RS2 v2.0 framework to the **go-forward, post-spin royalty company**, using the data pack as the starting point and web research to fill the gaps that the financial statements cannot: future cash-flow drivers, the status of material litigation, and the terms of the spin-off.

## SECTION 1 — BUSINESS & SOURCES OF VALUE

### The post-spin entity
- On **April 20, 2026**, AnaptysBio completed the taxable spin-off of First Tracks Biotherapeutics (TRAX), distributing 1 share of TRAX for every 1 share of ANAB to shareholders of record April 6, 2026 (BioSpace press release, 2026-04-20 [Actual]). TRAX received the pipeline and a $145M private placement; ANAB retains the financial collaborations.
- ANAB is now a **royalty-only company** with contractual passive revenue:
  - **Jemperli (dostarlimab)** — licensed to Tesaro, now GSK. ANAB receives tiered royalties: **8% on annual net sales below $1.0B, rising to 12% on the excess** (company IR, [Actual]; structure confirmed by a January 2026 press release: "tiered royalties of 8% for annual net sales below $1 billion and 12%…", with escalation provisions implied). In addition, ANAB has received **milestones**: $50M and $75M payments triggered when Jemperli crossed $1.0B in 2025 calendar-year sales (FirstWord Pharma, 2026 [Estimates confirming the triggers]).
  - **Imsidolimab** — licensed to Vanda Pharmaceuticals. ANAB earns **10% royalty on net sales**, up to $35M in regulatory/sales milestones, including $5M on U.S. FDA approval. **FDA PDUFA date for generalized pustular psoriasis: December 12, 2026** (Investing.com, 2026 [Estimate]).

### The litigation — the largest swing factor
- Pre-trial ruling in 2026 **preserved the current contracted royalty rates**, rejecting Tesaro/GSK's claim to slash them by 50% (FiercePharma, 2026 [Actual]; company IR [Actual]).
- The **July 14–17, 2026 Delaware Chancery trial** has been held; it adjudicates ANAB's claims that Tesaro/GSK committed material breaches, and ANAB's right to **full reversion of Jemperli rights** if breach is found (company IR [Actual]; TipRanks [Estimate]). Post-trial briefings run through **October 20, 2026**; a decision is pending as of T0 **[Unconfirmed outcome]**.

### Sources of value (post-spin)
1. Jemperli royalty cash flows (primary, ~95% of value).
2. Net cash: cash + short-term investments retained from the FY2025 balance sheet of $311M, less cash transferred to TRAX **[Unconfirmed split; assumption used below]**.
3. Imsidolimab option value (10% royalty + milestones).
4. Reversion optionality from the Delaware litigation.

- The >$390M at >$2.7B company statement implies an **effective rate of ~14.4% at or above ~$2.7B sales** `[Arithmetic]`.
- Conclusion: a **tiered schedule** (8% at current volumes, ramping to ~14.4% by ~$3B). This is the only structure consistent with *both* numbers and with the FY25 full-year revenue of $235M (8% × $1.128B = $90M + $75M Jemperli $1B milestone + ~$50M Q3-25 milestone + other ≈ $235M) `[Arithmetic]`.

**Moat and economics:** Royalty streams are contractual and have no marginal cost. Payer risk is GSK — investment-grade. The moat (the license agreement) is an **enforceable contract** — currently being tested in Delaware Chancery Court. Concentration is total: one drug provides essentially all revenue; one counterparty (GSK) pays it.

**Competition / industry demand:** Jemperli competes with Keytruda, Opdivo, and other PD-1s. But Anaptys does not *sell* the drug — GSK does. The relevant competitive question is whether Jemperli keeps winning share and expanding indications; GSK's Q1-26 print (+40% YoY) and dMMR endometrial share gains confirm a currently advantaged franchise. Peak sales beyond the $2.7B monotherapy guide depend on rectal cancer (AZUR-1, phase 2 data H2-2026), colon cancer (AZUR-2), and HNSCC (JADE) `[Actual — SEC Q3-25 release]`.
